target.name: Polar Semiconductor

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $700M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Polar Semiconductor is a growth-stage fabless semiconductor company that has raised $700M+ in total capital, including a 2024 recapitalization led by Niobrara Capital and Prysm Capital. The broader Chips & Semiconductors sector comprises 11 peer companies across public and private markets—including public benchmarks such as Anlogic, NVIDIA, and AMD, and private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and PsiQuantum—though the immediate comparable set for same-stage, similar-tier validation remains limited.

Given data constraints, stage-progression analysis represents the primary applicable triangulation method. Using the $700M total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for advancement from Growth stage, this method yields $840M. A peer-median approach was not executable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow peer universe; drawing on all-sector medians would introduce undue noise given Polar's specific market position.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $714M to $966M, with a median indication of $840M. This range reflects stage-progression logic anchored to historical capital deployment. Key uncertainties include the absence of granular recent trading or funding data for true-stage peers, the competitive and technology positioning relative to both public semiconductor leaders and private chip-design competitors, and macro conditions affecting capital availability in the sector. A single-method triangulation carries elevated range width and warrants validation through additional primary research.
